hypotheses.justification: The definition (line 316) is `chosenFiniteStepSymbol cell rep x = if hx : ∃ i, x ∈ cell i then rep (Classical.choose hx) else x`. In `Classical.choose {α} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ a, p a)` the predicate is `p_x = fun i => x ∈ cell i`. Take two points x, y that lie in exactly the same cells (∀ i, x ∈ cell i ↔ y ∈ cell i). Then `p_x = p_y` by `funext` and `propext`, and by proof irrelevance `Classical.choose hx = Classical.choose hy`. So `f x = f y`, even when the cells overlap. Hence f is constant on each atom `A_S = {x | ∀ i, x ∈ cell i ↔ i ∈ S}` with S ⊆ Fin n nonempty, and f = id on `A_∅`, the complement of `⋃ i, cell i`. There are finitely many atoms, and each is measurable because it is a finite intersection of the measurable sets `cell i` or their complements (from `hcell`). So f is measurable: for measurable B, `f ⁻¹' B = (A_∅ ∩ B) ∪ ⋃_{S ≠ ∅, c_S ∈ B} A_S`, where c_S is the constant value of f on A_S. You can also write f as a finite piecewise function of constants and `id` over these atoms and use `Measurable.piecewise`. The case n = 0 is trivial because then f = id. The existing proof uses `hdisj` only to rewrite f as an indicator sum. The argument above replaces that step, and the statement stays true and provable without `hdisj`.
